      "status": "examined-with-complete-retained-context",
      "summary": [
        "SMTP username storage now uses string preferences; the version63 migration rewrites nonempty stored values rejected by a strict UTF-8 decoder and preserves already-valid bytes, including its explicit old-truncation limit.",
        "Token builders encode usernames and the optional OAuth SASL frame separately from storage; LOGIN retains its preference-controlled Latin-1 branch when the credential fits in a byte.",
        "Literal-byte unit cases and migration fixtures check those branches, while the new SMTP scenario uses a changed, lenient fake server. Its shared transaction comparison still lacks an assertion message.",
        "No real server, OAuth/POP3 exchange, native migration or cryptographic result was tested, and later migration/backport phases remain separate."
